001package com.streamconverter.command.impl;
002
003import com.streamconverter.command.IStreamCommand;
004import java.io.IOException;
005import java.io.InputStream;
006import java.io.InputStreamReader;
007import java.io.OutputStream;
008import java.io.OutputStreamWriter;
009import java.io.PushbackReader;
010import java.io.Reader;
011import java.io.Writer;
012import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
013import java.util.Objects;
014import org.slf4j.Logger;
015import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory;
016
017/**
018 * Line ending normalization command.
019 *
020 * <p>This command normalizes line endings in text streams to a specified format. It can convert
021 * between different line ending styles (Unix LF, Windows CRLF, classic Mac CR) or preserve the
022 * input format.
023 *
024 * <p>The command processes data efficiently while preserving the exact structure of the input,
025 * including whether the input ends with a line terminator.
026 */
027public class LineEndingNormalizeCommand implements IStreamCommand {
028  private static final Logger logger = LoggerFactory.getLogger(LineEndingNormalizeCommand.class);
029
030  /** Supported line ending types for normalization. */
031  public enum LineEndingType {
032    /** Unix/Linux style line endings (LF only) */
033    UNIX("\n"),
034
035    /** Windows style line endings (CRLF) */
036    WINDOWS("\r\n"),
037
038    /** Classic Mac style line endings (CR only) - rarely used in modern systems */
039    MAC_CLASSIC("\r"),
040
041    /** Preserve input line endings as-is */
042    PRESERVE_INPUT(null),
043
044    /** Use system default line separator */
045    SYSTEM_DEFAULT(System.lineSeparator());
046
047    private final String separator;
048
049    LineEndingType(String separator) {
050      this.separator = separator;
051    }
052
053    /**
054     * Gets the line separator string for this type.
055     *
056     * @return the line separator string, or null for PRESERVE_INPUT
057     */
058    public String getSeparator() {
059      return separator;
060    }
061  }
062
063  private final LineEndingType targetType;
064
065  /**
066   * Creates a new line ending normalization command.
067   *
068   * @param targetType the target line ending type to convert to
069   * @throws NullPointerException if targetType is null
070   */
071  public LineEndingNormalizeCommand(LineEndingType targetType) {
072    this.targetType = Objects.requireNonNull(targetType, "Target type cannot be null");
073  }
074
075  @Override
076  public void execute(InputStream inputStream, OutputStream outputStream) throws IOException {
077    logger.debug("Starting line ending normalization to: {}", targetType);
078
079    // Stream processing for memory efficiency
080    try (Reader reader = new InputStreamReader(inputStream, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
081        Writer writer = new OutputStreamWriter(outputStream, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)) {
082
083      if (targetType == LineEndingType.PRESERVE_INPUT) {
084        copy(reader, writer);
085      } else {
086        normalize(reader, writer, targetType.getSeparator());
087      }
088
089      writer.flush();
090    }
091
092    logger.debug("Line ending normalization completed successfully");
093  }
094
095  private static void copy(Reader reader, Writer writer) throws IOException {
096    // For PRESERVE_INPUT, copy directly without modification
097    char[] buffer = new char[8192];
098    int charsRead;
099    // Stream the source as-is until the reader reaches EOF.
100    while ((charsRead = reader.read(buffer)) != -1) {
101      writer.write(buffer, 0, charsRead);
102    }
103  }
104
105  private static void normalize(Reader reader, Writer writer, String targetSeparator)
106      throws IOException {
107    // Process character by character for line ending normalization
108    PushbackReader pushbackReader = new PushbackReader(reader);
109    int current;
110    // Read one code unit at a time so CR, LF, and CRLF can be normalized consistently.
111    while ((current = pushbackReader.read()) != -1) {
112      if (current == '\r') {
113        handleCarriageReturn(pushbackReader, writer, targetSeparator);
114        continue;
115      }
116      if (current == '\n') {
117        writer.write(targetSeparator);
118        continue;
119      }
120      writer.write(current);
121    }
122  }
123
124  private static void handleCarriageReturn(
125      PushbackReader reader, Writer writer, String targetSeparator) throws IOException {
126    // Handle CR - could be CR, CRLF, or standalone CR
127    int next = reader.read();
128    writer.write(targetSeparator);
129    if (next != -1 && next != '\n') {
130      // The look-ahead character was not part of the line ending. Push it back so the
131      // main loop processes it; this keeps consecutive CRs (e.g. \r\r) handled as
132      // separate line endings instead of being written through as raw characters.
133      reader.unread(next);
134    }
135  }
136}
